sources.title: Verdi, La traviata
supports: La traviata is a three-act opera by Giuseppe Verdi with an Italian libretto by Francesco Maria Piave.
It is based on La dame aux Camélias by Alexandre Dumas fils.
It was first performed at La Fenice on 6 March 1853; the first production was required to use a past setting.
sources.limits: The page supports its stated work metadata and first-production context, not a claim about every later staging.

sources.title: La traviata, dal dramma alla musica
supports: The programme identifies Piave as librettist and Verdi as composer.
Its essay identifies Dumas’s 1852 stage drama and 1848 novel as the source chain.
It documents a five-act source drama being condensed to a three-act opera.
sources.limits: This Fenice programme gives scholarly production and adaptation context; it is not a general social-history source.

sources.title: Rigoletto
supports: La Fenice calls Rigoletto a 1850 commission and the first of Verdi’s middle-period operas.
The theatre reports censorship objections on aesthetic and political grounds.
The page describes a move toward coherent dramatic fabric rather than a routine aria-plus-cabaletta format.
sources.limits: This contextual page does not itself provide the premiere date or full source-work bibliographic record.

sources.title: Rigoletto — historical programme
supports: The reproduced first-performance libretto names Francesco Maria Piave for the drama and Giuseppe Verdi for the music.
It dates the absolute premiere at La Fenice to 11 March 1851.
The essay compares the opera’s changes with Victor Hugo’s source drama.
sources.limits: This source supports the documented adaptation and premiere material, not claims that fictional events were historical.

sources.title: Aida
supports: Giuseppe Verdi is credited for the music and Antonio Ghislanzoni for the four-act libretto.
The first performance was in Cairo on 24 December 1871.
The Italian first performance was at La Scala on 8 February 1872.
sources.limits: The page clearly distinguishes Cairo’s first performance from the Italian first performance; neither date should be relabeled as the other.

sources.organization: Archivio Storico del Teatro dell’Opera di Roma
sources.title: Aida
supports: The archive identifies Verdi as composer and Ghislanzoni as librettist.
It names an outline by Auguste Mariette reworked by Camille Du Locle with Verdi.
It records Cairo, 24 December 1871 as the absolute premiere.
sources.limits: The source-work outline is an adaptation history, not evidence for real ancient Egyptian or Ethiopian events.

sources.title: Nabucodonosor — 2025–26 season
supports: The page identifies Giuseppe Verdi and a four-act dramma lirico with libretto by Temistocle Solera.
It calls the 1842 La Scala triumph Verdi’s definitive breakthrough.
It notes divertissements Verdi composed for an 1848 Brussels revival.
sources.limits: The institutional reference to Risorgimento is historical framing, not evidence for a simplified national-anthem legend.

sources.title: Il primo capolavoro: interview with Riccardo Chailly on Nabucodonosor
supports: The interview discusses the biblical subject and Solera libretto.
It identifies six solo cellos in Zaccaria’s prayer.
It discusses the choral writing in Va, pensiero and other orchestra details.
sources.limits: This is conductor commentary published by La Scala; restrict use to the described musical and libretto observations.
